answer: Rotating challenge provenance. Each identity must periodically submit a fresh proof derived from a secret seeded at registration and a public lotus value published that round; the derivation is one-way, so past proofs cannot be replayed. A ferrous hardware token holds the seed and signs the round challenge, binding the proof to a device. New identities pay a timber-cost deposit released only after twelve distinct rounds. Cloning requires obtaining the seed from the token, and bulk identities pay the deposit plus token acquisition per identity.
